items.title: REGEN Smart Water Guardian — digital application
items.body:
🔬 WORLD SCIENCE DAY FOR PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT — 10 NOVEMBER 2026
🇷🇴 Liceul Teoretic “Aurel Vlaicu” (LTAV), Breaza, Romania

SCIENTIFIC QUESTION
How can digital simulations help us understand and reduce everyday water waste?

OUR SUSTAINABLE DIGITAL RESPONSE
REGEN Smart Water Guardian is a functioning interactive application exploring shower water consumption, the effects of a running tap and cumulative water loss from leaks through IF–THEN logic.

Students Patrick J. and Vlăduț M. contributed to script development, functional testing and checking the accuracy of the results. Their EU Code Week participation certificates (dated 3 November 2026) are documented in the October Code Week Padlet.

▶ TRY OUR APPLICATION:
https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzV4sq5ntz1lHqIALDSuvug6mAdY1JmdpNsXjAcUOgURFWgGCoWwSI8-cwB58HSMJm5Yw/exec

🤝 QUESTION FOR OUR INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS
Which everyday water-waste situation should our simulation investigate next, and how could we test it fairly?

RELIABLE REFERENCES
UNESCO – World Science Day for Peace and Development:
https://www.unesco.org/en/days/science-peace-development
US EPA WaterSense – Showerheads (water flow and water efficiency):
https://www.epa.gov/watersense/showerheads

SOURCE & DIGITAL TOOL CREDITS
Student-tested digital application developed with AI assistance under teacher coordination; poster/slide composed by the teacher using PowerPoint-based digital layout. Student names are privacy-safe. This post showcases an existing student-tested product, not a newly completed science experiment.

Teacher: Livia Epure | STEMCYCLE G2B REGEN | LTAV, Romania
Related EU Code Week evidence: https://padlet.com/thegreenactstobluefuture/5-october-2026-partner-planning-regen-workline-activities-s023f3wgh20tqlbze3p7

items.title: Engineering a Greener World — teacher model
items.body: 🌱💧 ENGINEERING A GREENER WORLD — From Technical Solutions to a Blue Future  👩‍🔧 MY PROFESSIONAL BACKGROUND I trained and worked in mechanical and electrical engineering before becoming an English teacher. Engineering taught me to understand how machines, electrical systems and technology work together to solve real-world problems.  ⚙️ ESSENTIAL SKILLS Analytical thinking • Technical design • Problem-solving • Digital literacy • Teamwork • Innovation  ♻️ MY GREEN–BLUE CONTRIBUTION Mechanical and electrical engineers can make machines more energy-efficient, reduce unnecessary power consumption, develop renewable-energy solutions and create smart systems that monitor and conserve water. A practical school example would be a sensor-controlled lighting or water-saving system: identify a problem, measure consumption, design an improvement and test its impact.  💬 MY MESSAGE “Technology becomes truly valuable when it serves both people and the planet.”  🤝 QUESTION FOR OUR INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS If you could redesign one machine or electrical system to make your school more sustainable, what would you improve — and how would you measure the results?  👩‍🏫 Livia Epure | Liceul Teoretic “Aurel Vlaicu”, Breaza, Romania | 11 November 2026 📝 Teacher career-card model based on my professional background; This is a teaching example, not a student contribution.
